item.title: Sydney man charged with car bomb plot and downloading Islamic State group material
item.description:
Sydney man charged with car bomb plot and downloading Islamic State group material
Australian police have arrested a man in the greater Sydney area on charges of researching how to build a car bomb and downloading violent material inspired by the Islamic State groupByROD MCGUIRK Associated PressNovember 20, 2026, 12:29 AM
MELBOURNE, Australia -- Australian police on Friday arrested a man in the greater Sydney area on charges of researching how to build a car bomb and downloading violent material inspired by the Islamic State group.
Police stressed they found no evidence of a link to the upcoming first anniversary of an IS-inspired attack at Sydney’s Bondi Beach. Two gunmen opened fire on a Dec. 14 Hanukkah celebration, leaving 15 people dead and 40 wounded.
Nowroz Rayed Amin, 35, from Ingleburn on Sydney’s southwestern outskirts, was charged with collecting documents likely to facilitate terrorist acts and possessing violent extremist material obtained online, Australian Federal Police Deputy Commissioner Hilda Sirec said.
“It will be alleged in court that the man was researching how to build a vehicle-borne, improvised explosive device, which we allege, for use in a potential terrorist act,” Sirec told reporters.
Amin appeared in the Campbelltown Local Court later Friday on the two charges, which carry a potential combined maximum penalty of 20 years in prison.
Amin did not enter pleas or apply for release on bail. He was remanded in custody to appear in court on Thursday next week, court documents show.
Investigators decided to make the arrest Friday because there was sufficient evidence and not because of any imminent threat to the community, according to Sirec, who said police suspected he had acted alone.

item.description:
Saudi Arabia intercepts more Yemen Houthi missiles and drones, and other Mideast news
Saudi Arabia says Iran-backed Houthi rebels have fired more missiles and drones at the kingdomByQASSIM ABDUL-ZAHRA Associated Press, FATMA KHALED Associated Press, and SAM METZ Associated PressNovember 20, 2026, 4:48 AM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
Saudi Arabia said on Friday that Iran-backed Houthi rebels fired more missiles and drones at the kingdom, days after it launched a major air campaign across Houthi-controlled parts of Yemen.
Meanwhile, in Iraq, troops deployed to a militia stronghold south of the capital Baghdad after the government apparently reached a compromise with a powerful Iran-backed militia it accused of smuggling oil.
Here is the latest news from the Middle East on Friday. Read our full coverage here.
Iraqi security forces set up a command headquarters on the outskirts of the Jurf al-Sakhar area south of Baghdad, long a stronghold of an Iran-backed militia, Kataib Hezbollah, on Friday.
The area had been the source of rising tensions, with the government calling for the militia to withdraw amid allegations that it was using the area for oil smuggling.
Kataib Hezbollah had threatened to fight security forces if they attempted an incursion.
Two Iraqi officials, speaking on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to comment publicly, said the government and Kataib Hezbollah had reached an agreement under which security forces could enter but the militia would not immediately withdraw.
The deal followed negotiations facilitated by Esmail Qaani, commander of Iran’s Quds Force, a branch of the paramilitary Revolutionary Guard that's responsible for operations outside Iran and is key to Iran’s influence and ties to allies across the Middle East.

item.title: Xi projects China’s global influence after hosting Trump and Putin at APEC
item.description:
Xi projects China’s global influence after hosting Trump and Putin at APEC
China’s President Xi Jinping has emerged from the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit with a diplomatic win, reinforcing his global standing despite limited substantive progressByHUIZHONG WU Associated Press and E. EDUARDO CASTILLO Associated PressNovember 20, 2026, 2:31 AM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
BANGKOK -- Results matter in the international arena, but so do optics. This week’s high-level meetings in China gave President Xi Jinping a win, reinforcing his image as a central player in global diplomacy.
As host of the annual Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen on Wednesday and Thursday, Xi welcomed the leaders of 21 nations representing some of the world’s largest economies that account for about 60% of global economic activity. He also convened the first formal gathering of the three biggest nuclear powers: the United States, Russia and China.
“History tells us that when major powers live in harmony, the world is at peace, and when they engage in confrontation the world is thrown into turmoil,” Xi said on Thursday before the start of closed-door discussions with U.S. President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
“Our three countries should set an example by working together to address global challenges, jointly safeguard world peace and stability and make greater contributions to human progress,” he added.
The summit in China's capital city was seen as emblematic of the nation's superpower status. The trilateral meeting on Thursday produced no major breakthroughs, but the image of the three leaders seated at an enormous round table with Xi at the center and Trump to his left and Putin to his right will become part of diplomatic history.

item.title: Russian missile crash in Poland likely an intentional provocation, Polish leader says
item.description:
Russian missile crash in Poland likely an intentional provocation, Polish leader says
Russian missile crash in Poland likely an intentional provocation as European militaries hold drills, Polish leader saysByThe Associated PressNovember 20, 2026, 5:30 AM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
WARSAW, Poland -- Russian missile crash in Poland likely an intentional provocation as European militaries hold drills, Polish leader says.
THIS IS AN APNewsAlert. Check back for updates. AP's earlier story is below.
The Polish military is investigating a “suspected violation” of the country's airspace near its border with Ukraine after officials sought to retrieve an unidentified object that had apparently crash-landed in Poland on Friday morning.
The incident came against the backdrop of Russian attacks in Ukraine that killed three people, injured nine others and damaged bridges and transport infrastructure. Polish Defense Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz said he believes the incident was another provocation by Russia and timed to European military exercises underway in Poland.
Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said he would convene a meeting with government ministers, military commanders and the head of security services in response. Officials said it was too early to tell what the object was.

item.title: Haiti strikes deal with El Salvador to build new prisons after minister visit
item.description:
Haiti strikes deal with El Salvador to build new prisons after minister visit
Haiti announces an agreement with El Salvador for the construction of a new prisonByEVENS SANON Associated Press, YOLANDA MAGAÑA Associated Press, and AND ANNA-CATHERINE BRIGIDA Associated PressNovember 20, 2026, 5:49 PM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
PORT-AU-PRINCE, Haiti -- Haiti announced an agreement with El Salvador Friday for the construction of new prisons as the two countries increase cooperation following the Central American country's deployment of troops to fight gangs in Haiti.
This announcement by Haitian Minister of Justice and Public Security Patrick Pélissier follows his official mission to El Salvador. The first prison will be launched soon with the prime minister ordering it to be expedited. It will be one of three prisons built by a Salvadoran company in collaboration with a Haitian firm, the minister said.
Gangs control an estimated 70% of Haiti’s capital and swaths of land in the country’s central region.
Pélissier praised the notorious Salvadoran maximum security prison CECOT, which he visited while in the Central American country for an international conference. El Salvador has been under a state of exception since 2022 that has imprisoned more than 90,000 people with no access to family visits. The U.S. has also deported Venezuelans and Salvadorans to the CECOT and they have denounced torture there after release.
“Once you enter, there is no hope of ever seeing the outside world again,” Pélissier said.
Haiti has struggled to find proper infrastructure to hold those arrested after powerful gangs raided the country’s two biggest prisons in 2024 and released thousands of inmates. Haiti's prisons have long been notorious for severe overcrowding, with human rights experts warning that prisoners sleep standing and hundreds have died in recent years. item.title: Bolivian festival seeks to return guinea pig to nations' rituals
item.description:
Bolivian festival seeks to return guinea pig to nations' rituals
Guinea pigs, known as cuy in the Andes region, have enjoyed a day in their honor in Bolivia with races, and beauty and weight contests, organized by students promoting the rodent’s nutritional and economic value to Bolivian householdsByCARLOS VALDEZ Associated PressNovember 20, 2026, 5:58 PM
Share
EL ALTO, Bolivia -- Guinea pigs, known as cuy in the Andes region, enjoyed a day in their honor Friday in Bolivia with races and beauty and weight contests organized by students promoting the rodent’s nutritional and economic value to Bolivian households.
Domesticated thousands of years ago in the Bolivian Andes, the cuy was considered sacred by ancient cultures and was used in ceremonies and as a food source. But raising them has nearly disappeared in recent decades as other meats have gained favor.
Students in the animal science and livestock program at the Public University of El Alto, a city neighboring La Paz, organized a race to reward the fastest cuy, a weigh-in to identify the heaviest and a runway show to crown the most stylish. The event brought together students and local farmers in the city, which sits at an elevation of 3,800 meters (12,500 feet).
“Our ancestors raised guinea pigs for centuries for food and rituals in the Andes,” said César Quispe, an instructor in the animal science program. “Their meat has high nutritional value and a low fat content.”
A cuy weighing 2.5 kilograms (5.5 pounds) from El Alto’s Kallutaca farm took the prize for the heaviest, while another from a different farm finished first in the speed race.
A food court offered a wide variety of traditional dishes, including roasted and baked cuys, cuys on skewers, and burgers and sausages made from the rodent’s meat.
Quispe said the decline of the cuy began during the colonial era, and today per capita consumption in Bolivia is low.

item.title: Russian attacks on Kyiv kill 3, cripple bridges and cut power
item.description:
Russian attacks on Kyiv kill 3, cripple bridges and cut power
Russia has launched missiles and drones across Kyiv, killing three people and injuring nineByThe Associated PressNovember 20, 2026, 3:31 AM
Share
KYIV, Ukraine -- Russia launched missiles and drones across Kyiv overnight that killed three people, injured nine others and damaged bridges and transport infrastructure, local authorities said Friday.
The attacks came hours after President Vladimir Putin vowed to retaliate against Ukraine for three aerial attacks this week on the vital Kerch Bridge, which links occupied Crimea with the Russian mainland.
“We will respond to these attacks, and I want everyone to be clear about that,” Putin told reporters Thursday in China, where he attended a summit with the Chinese and U.S. presidents. Putin said the road side of the bridge had been “seriously damaged” and vowed to rebuild.
The Kyiv City Military Administration said the attack struck four districts of the capital. The attack caused widespread electricity disruptions. Energy provider DTEK said parts of the Pecherskyi, Solomianskyi, Holosiivskyi, Dniprovskyi and Darnytskyi districts were without power following the strikes.
Non-residential buildings were damaged in the Obolonskyi and Holosiivskyi districts, while transport and logistics infrastructure was hit in the Podilskyi and Darnytskyi districts, it said in a statement.

item.title: El Salvador President Nayib Bukele seeks third term while attacking gangs in Haiti
item.description:
El Salvador President Nayib Bukele seeks third term while attacking gangs in Haiti
El Salvador’s President Nayib Bukele has officially launched his bid for reelection in the February electionsByYOLANDA MAGAÑA Associated Press and MEGAN JANETSKY Associated PressNovember 19, 2026, 10:15 PM
Share
SAN SALVADOR -- SAN SALVADOR (AP) — El Salvador President Nayib Bukele on Thursday night officially launched his candidacy for a third term in office after years of paving the way to stay in power indefinitely.
With virtually no political opposition, the highly popular leader is positioned to coast easily into a third term in office in the February elections. Recent polls put his approval ratings around 90%, largely due to his war on the country’s gangs. The crackdown, which began in 2022, has largely debilitated the criminal groups and sharply reduced violence but fueled accusations of mass human rights abuses.
The firebrand populist submitted his presidential candidate paperwork to the country’s Supreme Electoral Tribunal. His New Ideas party, which holds a supermajority in the country’s congress, cleared the way for him to be the party’s candidate in July and remain in power.
Crowds carrying “Bukele 2027” signs cheered his arrival in a fleet of police cars at the electoral tribunal building, where candidates for 60 congressional seats and 44 municipal council seats also submitted documentation ahead of the Thursday night deadline.
“In El Salvador there is total, complete open democracy,” an impassioned Bukele told roaring supporters. “We’re sending a message to the world that El Salvador will never return to the past.”
The reelection bid comes as Bukele has taken his crime offensive to Haiti. He deployed around 2,500 troops to fight gangs after the disappearance of four Salvadoran aviation technicians in an October gang attack.

item.title: France probes suspected leaks of confidential information to Le Pen’s far-right party
item.description:
France probes suspected leaks of confidential information to Le Pen’s far-right party
French authorities are investigating whether a former Interior Ministry official leaked confidential information to Marine Le Pen's far-right National RallyBySAMUEL PETREQUIN Associated PressNovember 20, 2026, 5:56 AM
Share
PARIS -- French authorities are investigating whether a former Interior Ministry official leaked confidential information about judicial investigations to Marine Le Pen' s far-right National Rally, adding to the party's legal troubles ahead of next year's presidential election.
Hugues Moutouh, a former general secretary in the ministry, is suspected of sharing information about investigations relating to the financing of the National Rally’s 2022 and 2024 election campaigns, according to Le Monde newspaper.
Moutouh now serves as prefect of the Centre-Val de Loire region, representing the central government there.
Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez confirmed Friday that a judicial investigation has been opened, and summoned Moutouh for a meeting.
The Paris prosecutor’s office confirmed to The Associated Press it opened a judicial investigation “into alleged breaches of professional confidentiality, breaches of investigative secrecy, and the handling of information obtained through these offences.” It said no one has been formally handed preliminary charges at this stage.
It added that investigators conducted searches at the party’s headquarters on Nov. 9.
Le Pen has not commented on the case.
“If the facts are confirmed, they are obviously very serious,” Nuñez told BFM TV.
